question: A 67-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of frequent urination overnight. He states that for several years he has had trouble maintaining his urine stream along with the need for frequent urination, but the nighttime urination has only recently started. The patient also states that he has had 2 urinary tract infections in the last year, which he had never had previously. On exam, his temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 124/68 mmHg, pulse is 58/min, and respirations are 13/min. On digital rectal exam, the prostate is enlarged but feels symmetric and smooth. Which of the following is a possible consequence of this condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Enlarged prostate -> urinary retention -> increased risk of urinary tract infections -> 80% CHAIN: Enlarged prostate -> obstructed urine flow -> increased residual urine volume -> increased risk of urinary tract infections -> 75% CHAIN: Enlarged prostate -> urinary stasis -> bacterial growth -> increased risk of urinary tract infections -> 70% CHAIN: Enlarged prostate -> urinary obstruction -> increased serum creatinine due to obstructive nephropathy -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of difficulty maintaining urine stream, frequent urination, and recent onset of nighttime urination along with an enlarged prostate suggest benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). BPH can lead to complications such as urinary tract infections due to incomplete bladder emptying. One possible consequence of BPH is increased serum creatinine due to obstructive uropathy and impaired kidney function.
